results.title: Camouflage in nature by pattern matching
results.brief_description: Explains how many animals bear protective colour patterns which blend with their variegated surroundings, thus providing a measure of protection. The film illustrates how those animals most needing protection, because of age, sex, or lack of ability to defend themselves, generally have subdued colouring. In contrast other animals, of a more offensive nature, have bold markings and dazzling effects.

results.title: Camera natura
results.creator_credit: Ross Gibson, John Cruthers, Australian Film Commission and Camera Natura
results.brief_description: A film about the Australian landscape as portrayed in the myths, maps, painting, writing, photography and cinema of white Australians. The video traces the developing image of the continent as it has been represented over 200 years, from the anguish of the convicted painter Thomas Watling, to the technologies of cinema and aerial photography. Written by Ross Gibson, cinematography by Ray Argall, animation by Lee Whitmore. Voices supplied by Stephen Bisley, Susan Dermody, Vivienne Garrett. Contains some black and white sequences.

results.title: Camera
results.creator_credit: Harris Watts, Mike Crisp and BBC
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “On camera: the BBC video production course”.
Consist of four parts: 1. The “Camera and the eye”. Shows the difficulties faced by the camera lens as compared by the eye and notes the advantages of the camera. 2. “Lenses and apertures”. Explains focal length, angle of view, depth of field, aperture openings, the times 2 extender and the gain switch. 3. “Short sizes and camera moves”. Explains basic terminology - such as pan, tilt, depress, track and zoom. 4. “Crossing the line” Shows how to mantain continuity of direction to avoid confusing the viewer.

results.title: Cambodia: Cambodia/Kampuchea
results.brief_description: This film exposes the nightmare of the revolution unleashed by Pol Pot’s Khmer Rouge after their victory in 1975. It explains the paranoia and provocation’s that led to the Vietnamese invasion; the famine, exodus and grinding war of resistance that followed; the struggle for peace in Kampuchea that continues to the present day … Cambodia/Kampuchea draws on unique propaganda film and archival material from the Khmer Rouge, Vietnam and other sources.
